claim.pdf_says: 12.4.6.3.2 General format:  APPLY COMMIT ON  [[ file-name-1][identifier-1]]...   — in the printed figure APPLY and COMMIT each carry an underline; ON carries no underline. (Preceding figure, 12.4.6.2: "I-O-CONTROL  .  [ [ apply-commit-clause] . ]   [[{ same-clause }...].]" — I-O-CONTROL is underlined.)
claim.markdown_says:
```
APPLY COMMIT ON  [[ file-name-1][identifier-1]]…
```
(and, above it, "```\nI-O-CONTROL . [ [ apply-commit-clause] . ]  [[ { same-clause } …].]\n```") — both figures are plain code blocks with no <u> markup and no "Figure notes" paragraph, so no underlining information survives.
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is normative in a general format: underlined uppercase words are required words, non-underlined uppercase words are optional words. With the underlines dropped, the markdown APPLY COMMIT ON reads as three required keywords when ON is optional — the falsely-restrictive-syntax failure mode this sweep is hunting. Every other general format in this batch preserves the distinction: pages 349, 355, 357, 359, 361 and 365 each carry an explicit "Figure notes" paragraph naming which words are underlined, and page 365 Formats 1 and 2 use inline <u>SAME</u> / <u>RECORD</u> markup. Page 363 is the only figure-bearing page in the batch that records neither.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent render + pixel measurement, not by eyeballing alone.

(1) Both quotes are accurate. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 15660 is byte-for-byte `APPLY COMMIT ON  [[ file-name-1][identifier-1]]…` inside a bare ``` fence, and line 15643 is `I-O-CONTROL . [ [ apply-commit-clause] . ]  [[ { same-clause } …].]`, also a bare fence. Neither carries <u> markup, and there is no "Figure notes" paragraph anywhere between the 12.4.6 heading (line 15632) and the 12.4.6.3.3 Syntax rules heading (line 15664). The work-unit slice E:/Temp/specrecon/v363/page-363.md matches the committed transcription exactly, so this is the real transcription, not a re-extraction artifact.

(2) The printed glyphs, measured rather than guessed. On the 2550x3300 300-dpi render of spec_p363.png the 12.4.6.3.2 figure line occupies y=1796..1835. Its word groups by x-extent are: APPLY (605-732), COMMIT (755-933), ON (955-1011), then `[[` (1044-1071) and the lowercase nonterminals (1090-1672). The underline rule sits on a single scanline y=1841 and consists of EXACTLY TWO dark runs: x=599-737 and x=758-937. Those align to APPLY and COMMIT respectively (each rule overhangs its word by ~5 px, the normal PDF underline lead-in). There is NO run of any length over x=955-1011. So ON is unambiguously not underlined — this is not a faint rule, a thin rule, or a rule clipped by the crop; the scanline is empty there. Likewise the 12.4.6.2 figure's only underline is at y=1010-1011, x=389-644, under `I-O-CONTROL` alone.

(3) The normative significance is the spec's own, stated twice. §5.2.2 Keywords (line 2628): keywords "are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword". §5.2.3 Optional words (line 2641): optional words "are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity". Restated at lines 5770 and 5805. So the printed figure says APPLY and COMMIT are required and ON is optional — `APPLY COMMIT file-name-1` is legal source — while the markdown figure conveys no required/optional information at all and reads as three mandatory keywords.

(4) This is a gap in the transcription's own convention, not a global formatting choice that could be waived as mere styling. The transcription carries 225 "Figure notes" paragraphs specifically to preserve underlining, and does so on both immediate neighbours: the SHARING clause figure on page 361 (line 15613: "`WITH` and `OTHER` are **not** underlined — they are optional words") and the SAME clause on page 365, which uses inline `<u>SAME</u>` / `<u>RECORD</u>` (lines 15739, 15743) plus a Figure notes paragraph for Format 3 (line 15753, which explicitly records "`AREA` and `FOR` are not underlined"). Page 363 is the one figure-bearing page in this stretch that records neither. Nothing elsewhere in 12.4.6.3 recovers the information: Syntax rules 1-11 and General rules 1-6 never mention ON, and the sole worked example (line 42050, `APPLY COMMIT ON STCK-FILE CHNG-FILE UPDATE-COUNT.`) writes ON, so it cannot discriminate optional from required.

Rejection tests all fail to fire: the underlining is not present-but-reflowed (there is no markup and no notes paragraph anywhere on the page), it is not page-break furniture or wrapping, the claim misquotes neither source, and it does change meaning — required vs. optional word is a syntax-legality difference.
verdict.corrected_description:
The finding is real and the claim's substance is accurate; two refinements to its scope.

SCOPE NARROWING: only the 12.4.6.3.2 figure suffers an actual normative loss. In the 12.4.6.2 I-O-CONTROL figure the underlined word `I-O-CONTROL` is the ONLY uppercase word present — every other element is a lowercase nonterminal (`apply-commit-clause`, `same-clause`) or punctuation — so dropping its underline creates no required/optional ambiguity, and §5.2.9 already makes the separator period required regardless. Treat 12.4.6.2 as cosmetic and 12.4.6.3.2 as the normative defect.

THE DEFECT, precisely: in the printed 12.4.6.3.2 general format, `APPLY` and `COMMIT` are underlined (required words per §5.2.2) and `ON` is printed WITHOUT an underline (an optional word per §5.2.3), so `APPLY COMMIT file-name-1` is legal source with ON omitted. Verified at 300 dpi: the underline scanline y=1841 has exactly two runs, x=599-737 (APPLY, glyphs 605-732) and x=758-937 (COMMIT, glyphs 755-933), and no run at all beneath the ON glyphs at x=955-1011. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 15660 renders the figure as a bare code fence with no <u> markup and no "Figure notes" paragraph, losing the distinction entirely and presenting ON as a third required keyword.

FIX: add a Figure notes paragraph after line 15661 reading, e.g. "> **Figure notes (APPLY COMMIT clause general format).** `APPLY` and `COMMIT` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). `ON` is **not** underlined — it is an optional word. `file-name-1` and `identifier-1` are not underlined. The nested brackets with the trailing ellipsis permit one or more file-names and/or identifiers, subject to SR 4 (at least one file or data-item shall be specified)." Optionally also note that `I-O-CONTROL` is underlined in the 12.4.6.2 figure, for uniformity with the surrounding pages.

NO LIVE COMPILER BUG YET: `APPLY`/`APPLY COMMIT` appears in no `.g4` fragment under src/, so the clause is unimplemented and nothing currently mis-requires ON. The defect is forward-looking — it would seed a falsely-restrictive grammar the moment the I-O-CONTROL paragraph is implemented from the transcription.
